report.summary: Chunk 5 of correctness.py: defines evaluate_change (continuation), verify_before_state, _slug, load_correctness_tasks, save_correctness_tasks, run_corpus, _changed_files, _blob, _test_functions. Claims about behaviour are checked against visible code.
risks: evaluate_change line 1121-1188 | medium | The function returns early with finish() for various errors, but the finish function is not defined in this chunk; correctness of early returns depends on external finish. | Verify finish() definition in same module.

evaluate_change line 1167-1170 | medium | The except clause catches Exception (noqa BLE001) and returns finish with a generic message; this may hide unexpected exceptions. | Confirm that this broad catch is intentional and safe.

verify_before_state line 1198-1199 | low | The docstring says 'Used when seeding a corpus. A candidate task that does not survive this is reported...' but the function returns a BeforeState, not a report; the reporting is external. | Check caller to see if reporting happens.
run_corpus line 1317-1336 | low | The function uses load_correctness_tasks() as default tasks, but this may cause side effects (reading file) if called with default. | Ensure this is intended.

_test_functions line 1351-1388 | low | The function uses ast.get_source_segment which may return None; fallback to ast.dump is provided, but dump output may not be source. | Acceptable as fallback, but note potential difference.
todos: Consider adding explicit type annotations to local variables for clarity.
Ensure finish() is defined and handles all outcome strings correctly.
Verify that _check_selection returns a string or None; the code uses boolean context (if moved:) which works if it returns '' or None.
Check that judge_before_state and judge_after_state are defined and return objects with .unrunnable, .verified, .reasons etc.

handoff.purpose: Defines the core evaluation loop (evaluate_change continuation), before-state verification, corpus I/O, corpus self-validation, and history-seeding helpers.

claims.text: FROZEN HERE -- before the worktree exists, before the overlay, and long before any candidate bytes are applied. Everything below reads this object; nothing below reads `task` for a node id again.
claims.why: The comment is accurate: selection = freeze_selection(task, base, timeout_s) occurs before worktree creation. Subsequent code uses selection, not task, for node ids.

claims.text: REPORTED as invalid, never silently dropped and never counted as a pass -- the same rule mint.py applies to a vacuous label.
claims.why: The comment describes behaviour (reported, not silently dropped) that is not verifiable from this code alone; depends on how finish() and caller handle OUTCOME_TASK_INVALID.

claims.text: SAME frozen selection, deliberately: the after run measures exactly what was declared before the change existed.
claims.why: The code reuses the same selection variable for the after run; no new freeze_selection call.

claims.text: Used when seeding a corpus. A candidate task that does not survive this is reported, with its reasons, and not admitted -- which is the measurement that says how much a corpus is worth.
claims.why: The function returns a BeforeState; reporting and admission logic is in the caller, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Read the corpus, or ``[]`` if it does not exist yet. Sorted by id.
claims.why: Code checks os.path.exists(p) and returns [] if not; then sorts by 'id'.

claims.text: Overwrite the corpus. Deterministic formatting, same contract as ``harness.write_baseline`` / ``mint.save_minted_tasks``.
claims.why: The claim about same contract as harness/mint is not verifyable from this chunk; the function does write deterministic JSON (sorted keys, indent).

claims.text: Evaluate every task against its OWN reference patch. The corpus's own gate.
claims.why: Code calls evaluate_change(task, use_reference=True) for each task.

claims.text: This is the corpus validating ITSELF: a task whose reference fix does not produce ``fixed`` is not a task, and an evaluator that cannot show that its corpus discriminates is in the same position as the pytest gate it exists to strengthen.
claims.why: The philosophical claim about 'corpus validating itself' is not checkable from code; the code does produce a 'discriminates' field.

claims.text: Counts are reported per outcome and NEVER blended into a single 'score' -- ``task_invalid`` and ``could_not_run`` in particular are not failures of the change, and folding them into one number would hide exactly the distinction this module was built for.
claims.why: The function returns a 'counts' dict per outcome and a 'discriminates' boolean; it does not compute a blended score.

claims.text: {pytest node-id suffix -> that test's source}, for one Python test file.
claims.why: The function returns a dict mapping node-id strings to source code strings.

claims.text: The key is the node id form pytest actually accepts -- ``test_x`` for a module-level function, ``ClassName::test_x`` for a method -- because the class qualifier is not optional and getting it wrong makes the node id ``missing``.
claims.why: The code builds keys as node.name for module-level and f'{node.name}::{child.name}' for methods.

claims.text: That is not a hypothetical: the first run of this seeder used unqualified names from ``structcore.extract_units`` (which reports a method as a bare ``test_alive_then_stale``) and the before-state check refuted 19 of 22 candidate nodes in one commit for exactly that reason.
claims.why: Historical anecdote; cannot be verified from this code.

claims.text: ``ast`` rather than a regex or the structural extractor: it is stdlib, it is exact about nesting, and pytest node ids are a Python-only concept anyway. A file that does not parse contributes nothing (the caller then mints nothing from it) rather than contributing guesses.
claims.why: The function uses ast.parse and returns {} on SyntaxError.

observations.what: evaluate_change uses a broad except Exception clause (noqa BLE001) that catches any exception during the after-run setup and returns OUTCOME_COULD_NOT_RUN with a generic message.

The function verify_before_state returns BeforeState with base_label or base inconsistently: on line 1198 it returns BeforeState(False, base_label, ...), on line 1202 it returns BeforeState(False, base, ...) where base is a resolved revision (sha?), not a label.
In verify_before_state, the docstring says 'Used when seeding a corpus', but the function does not perform any seeding or reporting; it only returns state.
The function _slug uses re.sub on str(text).lower() but text may not be a string; task.get('id') could be non-string.
run_corpus uses load_correctness_tasks() as default, which reads a file; if called without arguments, it has a side effect of reading from disk.
The function _changed_files uses _git_read but _git_read is not defined in this chunk; assumes it exists.
The function _test_functions uses ast.get_source_segment which may return None; fallback to ast.dump may produce non-source representation.
